question: What is the main goal of preparing a modified-texture diet for a patient with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia)?

options.A: To eliminate all sodium and fats from daily caloric intake
options.B: To reduce the visual appeal of food so the patient eats less
options.C: To increase the speed of carbohydrate digestion in the stomach
options.D: To prevent the risk of choking and aspiration during swallowing

explanation: Changing food consistency makes swallowing safe, protecting the patient's airway from food or liquid going down the wrong pipe.

question: What is a key nursing priority when caring for a patient newly diagnosed with a uterine issue causing recurrent miscarriages?

options.A: Explaining that lifestyle choices are the sole cause of her congenital condition
options.B: Discouraging her from asking questions about future pregnancy attempts
options.C: Providing empathetic emotional support alongside clear education about treatment options
options.D: Insisting that the patient undergo immediate major surgery to remove the uterus

explanation: Spot on, nurse! This diagnosis can be heartbreaking. Patients need a compassionate ear just as much as they need clear, easy-to-understand medical facts.

question: What is the number one direct cause of maternal death all over the world?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the leading global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH can literally save a life!

question: What is a main objective of setting clinical standards in Quality Assurance?

options.A: Ensuring every nurse performs procedures the same safe way
options.B: Making sure doctors do all the documentation
options.C: Eliminating the need for patient handovers
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing shifts per week

explanation: Spot on! Clinical standards act like a reliable compass. They make sure that no matter who is on duty, every patient gets the same safe, top-notch care.

question: How should you respond when a client uses unhealthy coping tricks like total denial or locking themselves away from others?

options.A: Immediately discharge the client from home care services
options.B: Ignore the behavior because it will naturally resolve itself
options.C: Confront the behaviors with empathy rather than harsh judgment
options.D: Scold the client for failing to follow the rehabilitation plan

explanation: Harshness pushes people further into their shell. Meeting them with patience and understanding gives them a safe space to start healing emotionally.

question: What does 'patient autonomy' mean in reproductive healthcare?

options.A: The requirement that family elders approve all medical procedures
options.B: The right of the individual to make self-determining choices about their body
options.C: The legal authority of the healthcare provider to choose the best treatment
options.D: The financial independence of the hospital from government oversight

explanation: Autonomy simply means it is the patient's body and their choice. Every individual has the right to decide what happens to their own medical care.

question: Why do disaster survivors often experience severe psychological distress alongside physical injuries?

options.A: Because the sudden event shatters their sense of safety and security
options.B: Because medication given in hospitals always causes anxiety
options.C: Because disaster victims rarely have family members nearby
options.D: Because physical pain stops the brain from thinking clearly

explanation: Disasters violently disrupt the predictable routines and safety nets that people rely on to feel secure in the world. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is the main goal of medications used to treat autoimmune diseases?

options.A: To permanently eliminate all white blood cells from the body
options.B: To suppress the hyperactive immune response and reduce inflammation
options.C: To cure the genetic mutation that caused the disease
options.D: To replace lost body fluids during an acute infection

explanation: These drugs act like a calm-down pill for an overactive immune system, stopping it from attacking healthy tissues.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four legal elements needed to prove professional negligence?

options.A: Actual damages suffered by the patient
options.B: Direct causation of an injury
options.C: Guaranteed hospital bankruptcy
options.D: Breach of the legal duty of care

explanation: You got it! Hospital bankruptcy is just a financial state—it has nothing to do with the legal checklist needed to prove negligence in court.

question: What is a mandatory safety action when a newborn is receiving phototherapy?

options.A: Keeping the incubator lights turned off at all times
options.B: Covering the infant's eyes with protective patches
options.C: Applying heavy moisturizing lotion to the skin every hour
options.D: Wrapping the baby tightly in warm blankets to prevent chills

explanation: Always make sure the baby's eyes are securely covered with eye patches to protect their delicate retina from the bright phototherapy lights. Safety first!

question: Why do some women still seek out traditional practitioners for gishiri cuts instead of going to a hospital?

options.A: Government policy requires trying traditional methods first
options.B: Hospitals mandate the procedure for all pregnant women
options.C: Traditional healers offer free antibiotics and modern anesthesia
options.D: Cultural beliefs strongly link reproductive issues to a traditional diagnosis

explanation: Deeply ingrained cultural norms and traditional explanations for illnesses drive patients toward local healers before or instead of formal health facilities. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h2)

question: How do staff shortages at primary health centers negatively affect immunization coverage?

options.A: Clinics are forced to close permanently on weekends
options.B: Vaccines automatically expire faster due to lack of supervision
options.C: Patients are charged higher official fees for every injection
options.D: Nurses have less time for community outreach and tracking defaulters

explanation: Spot on! When nurses are overworked with heavy patient loads, community visits and following up on missed doses get left behind.

question: What is the main result when a genetic mutation affects a receptor?

options.A: The receptor becomes misshapen, altering normal hormone response
options.B: The hormone itself changes into a dangerous chemical toxin
options.C: The blood supply to the target endocrine gland is cut off
options.D: The cell membrane immediately dissolves into the bloodstream

explanation: A genetic typo changes the building blocks of the receptor protein, making its shape wonky so it doesn't fit the hormone key quite right. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main difference between a mechanical bowel obstruction and a functional ileus?

options.A: A mechanical obstruction causes no pain, while an ileus causes severe cramps
options.B: A mechanical obstruction has a physical block, while an ileus happens when bowel movement simply stops without a block
options.C: An ileus is caused by scar tissue, while a mechanical obstruction is caused by high sugar
options.D: A mechanical obstruction affects only the colon; an ileus affects only the stomach

explanation: A mechanical block is something physical like a tumor or scar tissue getting in the way. An ileus is lazy bowel—the muscles just pause their normal movement without any physical wall.

question: Why do nurses commonly use compresses in the ward?

options.A: To lower a patient's overall core body temperature rapidly
options.B: To replace the need for intravenous fluid resuscitation
options.C: To permanently cure chronic autoimmune joint diseases
options.D: To provide localized pain relief and reduce inflammation

explanation: Compresses are great for targeting one specific spot to ease pain and bring down swelling, rather than treating the whole body.

question: What does the principle of equity mean in public health?

options.A: Fair distribution of health resources to close gaps between different groups
options.B: Giving every single hospital the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Providing identical medical treatments to every patient regardless of age
options.D: Ensuring doctors earn the same salary as community health workers

explanation: Equity means giving fair opportunities and resources based on need so that everyone has a fair chance at good health, especially vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which friendly bacteria is most commonly found keeping a healthy reproductive-age vagina happy and protected?

options.A: Staphylococcus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Streptococcus
options.D: Lactobacillus

explanation: Lactobacillus is our hero bug here! It's the dominant, protective bacterium that keeps the vaginal environment healthy and balanced. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, morbidity, and mortality
options.B: Vector, reservoir, and transmission
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Primary, secondary, and tertiary

explanation: Think of disease as a puzzle made of three pieces: the germ (agent), the person (host), and where they live (environment).

question: What is the main goal of inferential statistics in nursing research?

options.A: To draw pictures and graphs of patient medical records
options.B: To make guesses about a large group based on a small study group
options.C: To calculate the exact average age of patients in a single ward
options.D: To store patient health history in a computer database

explanation: Spot on! Since we can't study every single patient in Nigeria, we use a smaller group (sample) to draw conclusions about the wider population. You've got this!

question: What critical warning sign must you teach a patient who is taking hormonal reproductive medications?

options.A: Temporary fatigue in the evening
options.B: Sudden chest pain or leg swelling
options.C: Mild changes in hair texture
options.D: Slight increase in daily appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Hormones can raise the risk of blood clots, so chest pain or a swollen leg are major red flags patients must report immediately.

question: Why might a very stressed or anxious mum find it hard to express milk?

options.A: Stress permanently destroys the lactiferous ducts inside the breast
options.B: Anxiety causes the anterior pituitary to completely stop making prolactin
options.C: Nerve impulses from the nipple travel backward during panic attacks
options.D: Adrenaline constricts blood vessels and interferes with oxytocin release

explanation: You're doing great! Stress releases adrenaline, which gets in the way of oxytocin and makes the milk harder to let down. Relaxation is key!

question: What is the best way to determine a patient's prior knowledge about a new medication?

options.A: Asking open-ended questions
options.B: Ordering a blood electrolyte panel
options.C: Reading their bank statements
options.D: Checking their vital signs

explanation: Open-ended questions invite patients to share what they understand in their own words without feeling tested. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h3)

question: When a patient says 'ah', the nurse notices the uvula shifts to one side and the gag reflex is weak. Which nerves are likely involved?

options.A: Cranial nerves XI and XII
options.B: Cranial nerves I and II
options.C: Cranial nerves IX and X
options.D: Cranial nerves III and IV

explanation: You're doing great! Nerves IX and X team up to manage the throat, swallowing, and our gag reflex.

question: Which of these statements about nursing leadership is FALSE?

options.A: It is built by taking on small projects and precepting students.
options.B: It is a continuous developmental journey throughout a career.
options.C: It can be cultivated through mentorship and continuing education.
options.D: It is an innate trait that cannot be learned or improved over time.

explanation: Leadership isn't a rare magic power you are born with! Anyone can grow and improve their leadership skills over time through practice, learning, and good mentors.

question: Why should nurses encourage elderly residents to do parts of their own bath and hygiene care?

options.A: To preserve their dignity and functional independence
options.B: To lower the financial cost of facility operations
options.C: To eliminate the need for any assistive devices
options.D: To reduce the workload of the nursing staff completely

explanation: You got it! Doing things for themselves—even small tasks—helps residents keep their strength and feel good about their independence.

question: What is gender discrimination in community health primarily based on?

options.A: Family income level and education
options.B: Geographical location of residence
options.C: Biological sex or gender identity
options.D: Professional occupation and status

explanation: Gender discrimination is specifically rooted in bias against an individual's biological sex or how they identify in terms of gender. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h1)

question: Which dietary combination helps your body absorb non-heme (plant-based) iron better?

options.A: Iron with raw grains
options.B: Iron with black coffee
options.C: Iron with heavy dairy
options.D: Iron with Vitamin C

explanation: Awesome! Pairing your plant iron with a splash of Vitamin C (like orange juice or lemon) gives your gut a big boost in absorbing it.

question: Why is a Pap smear so important when you spot a red patch on the cervix?

options.A: To chemically destroy the extra columnar cells on the surface
options.B: To measure the exact hormonal levels circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: To rule out malignant or pre-cancerous changes that can look similar to benign erosion
options.D: To prove that the patient has an active bacterial infection

explanation: Harmless ectropion can sometimes look very similar to early cellular changes or cancer. A Pap smear helps us be 100% sure the patient is safe.

question: What is a major ethical duty of a nurse leader when there are too few nurses on duty?

options.A: Ordering existing staff to work double shifts indefinitely
options.B: Hiding the shortage from hospital executives to avoid trouble
options.C: Reducing the quality of care documentation to save time
options.D: Advocating for corrective action to protect patient safety

explanation: Patient safety comes first! Leaders have a duty to speak up to management when short-staffing threatens safe care.

question: Why do doctors prescribe anticholinergic medications for urinary symptoms?

options.A: To relax the bladder and increase holding capacity
options.B: To kill bacteria causing urinary tract infections
options.C: To shrink an enlarged prostate gland
options.D: To stimulate bladder contractions during voiding

explanation: These drugs stop the bladder from going into sudden spasms, meaning your patient can hold more urine without that emergency rush to the toilet.

question: Which oxygen delivery device provides the most precise and controlled oxygen concentration?

options.A: Non-rebreather mask
options.B: Standard nasal cannula
options.C: Simple face mask
options.D: Venturi mask

explanation: The Venturi mask uses interchangeable adapters to mix exact amounts of room air with oxygen, delivering a very specific percentage of gas. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h3)

question: What makes an adverse drug reaction (ADR) different from a medication error?

options.A: An ADR happens even when the correct dose and drug are given.
options.B: An ADR is caused by the pharmacist giving the wrong medication.
options.C: An ADR only occurs if the nurse administers the drug too fast.
options.D: An ADR only happens during an intentional drug overdose.

explanation: You've got this! An ADR happens unexpectedly even when you do everything right with the dose and drug, unlike a dosage mistake.

question: If a local government wants to reduce rabies cases in humans, what should they prioritize first?

options.A: Draining all local ponds and slow-moving irrigation streams
options.B: Conducting a mass vaccination campaign for domestic dogs
options.C: Providing free insecticide-treated nets to market traders
options.D: Issuing strict travel bans on all livestock transport vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Since dogs are the main carrier of rabies, vaccinating them directly protects us from exposure.

question: How do good communication skills help families stay healthy?

options.A: They dictate strict financial rules for family members
options.B: They reduce conflict and help members express needs clearly
options.C: They ensure that arguments never happen in any household
options.D: They replace the need for physical health checkups

explanation: When family members talk openly and listen well, they solve problems faster and keep peace in the home.

question: What is the main cause of communicable (spreadable) diseases?

options.A: Genetically inherited cellular mutations
options.B: Nutritional deficiencies in the diet
options.C: Long-term exposure to industrial chemicals
options.D: Infectious agents like bacteria and viruses

explanation: You nailed it! Communicable diseases are caused by tiny living germs like bacteria and viruses that can pass from one person to another.

question: Which teaching principle means we should start with what matters most to the patient right now?

options.A: Repetition
options.B: Active participation
options.C: Relevance
options.D: Strict discipline

explanation: You got it! When we talk about things that touch their daily lives and immediate worries, patients listen and learn much faster.

question: What do high levels of AST and ALT on a blood test usually mean?

options.A: Rapid regeneration of healthy liver tissue
options.B: Active injury and damage to liver cells
options.C: An infection located within the urinary bladder
options.D: Inadequate intake of dietary proteins

explanation: When liver cells get stressed or damaged, these internal enzymes (AST and ALT) leak out into the bloodstream like a distress signal.

question: What is the main goal of a health screening test?

options.A: To provide a definitive and final medical diagnosis
options.B: To replace the need for primary prevention vaccines
options.C: To cure a chronic illness without needing further treatment
options.D: To identify unrecognized disease in apparently healthy people

explanation: Screenings help us catch hidden health issues early in people who feel completely fine, giving them a head start on care.

question: What happens to the pelvic joints to help the baby pass through the birth canal during labor?

options.A: They yield and allow slight widening of the pelvic ring.
options.B: They lock firmly in place to protect the spinal cord.
options.C: They shrink in size to push the baby downward.
options.D: They temporarily fuse into a single solid bone.

question: Which principle of primary health care ensures that vulnerable populations receive care regardless of wealth?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Centralization
options.C: Technological advancement
options.D: Specialization

explanation: Equity ensures fair distribution of health services so that vulnerable groups are not left behind. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h2)

question: How are health outcomes usually measured in a Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: Natural clinical units like life-years gained or blood pressure lowered
options.B: Subjective happiness scales completely unrelated to physical health
options.C: Monetary amounts such as dollars or naira earned by the hospital
options.D: Total number of staff employed in the outpatient department

explanation: Instead of money, cost-effectiveness looks at real clinical results—like millimeters of mercury dropped in blood pressure or extra years of life gained.

question: Which of these is a classic geriatric syndrome often managed in long-term care?

options.A: Acute appendicitis
options.B: Bacterial meningitis
options.C: Pressure injuries
options.D: Compound fractures

question: Why is understanding a patient's home environment vital for a successful care plan?

options.A: It allows the nurse to charge appropriate hospital fees
options.B: It replaces the need for any physical assessment
options.C: It ensures the recommended treatment is realistic for their daily life
options.D: It prevents family members from visiting the ward

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing what life looks like at home helps us design treatment plans the patient can actually afford and manage.

question: What is gluten's main job when baking bread and pastries?

options.A: It acts as a primary artificial sweetener
options.B: It preserves food against bacterial spoilage
options.C: It gives dough elasticity and chewy texture
options.D: It adds essential vitamin C to baked goods

explanation: Think of gluten as the stretchy protein network that traps gases, giving bread its lovely bounce and structure!

question: What is the primary purpose of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: Recruiting new nursing staff for the facility
options.B: Monitoring performance and taking corrective action
options.C: Assigning daily bedside duties to junior nurses
options.D: Drafting the annual financial budget for the hospital

explanation: Controlling is primarily about tracking actual work against set plans and fixing mistakes when things go wrong. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)
